faq: How much traffic do I need for a test?
More traffic gives clearer answers. If your store has low traffic, we tell you before starting and pick bigger changes that show a result sooner, rather than tiny tweaks.
Which testing tool do you use?
We use what suits your platform and budget, often a free or low-cost tool or built-in theme tests. You see the monthly cost before we install anything.
Will you promise a winning result?
No. A test can show that a change helps, does nothing or hurts. All three are useful, because you learn what your shoppers respond to without changing the whole store.
Does the test slow down my store?
We pick lightweight methods and check speed before and after. If a tool adds noticeable delay, we change method.

desc:
A/B testing setup for ecommerce stores means showing two versions of one page element to different shoppers and keeping the one that performs better. Ecom Swift LLC plans, builds and tracks the test in your own store, then explains the result in plain language.

## What is A/B testing in an online store?

A/B testing is a controlled comparison. Half of your visitors see the current version of a page, the other half see a changed version, and your analytics record which group buys more. Because both groups browse at the same time, seasons and ad spend affect both equally, so the difference you see is far more likely to come from the change itself.

## Why guessing costs you more than testing

Every store owner has opinions about button colors, hero images and price layouts. Acting on the wrong one can quietly lower your conversion rate for months before anyone notices. A test turns an argument into an observation, and what you learn can be applied to every product page, not only the one you tested.

## How testing affects conversions and revenue

A test works because it isolates one variable. If the new version of an add to cart area produces more orders per visitor, that gain repeats on every future visit. A small improvement on a page that thousands of people see adds up to a meaningful change in orders.

Honesty matters here. Small stores often do not have enough visitors to reach a clear answer quickly, and a test that ends too early can point you the wrong way. We plan the test length around your real traffic and tell you when a result is still too close to call.

## What a well-run test includes

- One clear question, such as whether a shorter headline leads to more add to cart clicks.
- A single change per test, so the result has one explanation.
- Two versions built in your store without breaking the layout on phones.
- A fair traffic split, with each visitor seeing the same version on every return visit.
- A primary goal chosen before the test starts, such as purchases or add to cart events.
- Goal tracking confirmed with a real test order or click.
- A written start date and a planned end date, so nobody stops early on a lucky day.
- A note of anything else that changed during the run, like a sale or a new ad campaign.
- A read-out that states the result, how sure we are and what to do next.
- A simple record of ideas for later tests, ranked by effort and likely value.

## How we run your test

First we look at your store and your analytics and agree on one change worth testing. Good candidates are headlines, button text, image order, price display, shipping messages and the placement of trust details.

Next we build both versions in your own account and connect the goal in your analytics. We check both versions on phone and desktop, run a test purchase, and then switch the test on. While it runs we watch for technical problems, not for a winner.

When the test has enough data, we send a short note with what happened. The Basic package covers one planned and launched test. The Standard package adds a second test and a read-out of the results so far. The Premium package adds a ranked list of test ideas, separate testing on mobile and desktop and a planning call. Add-ons such as a heat map or a formal report are available if you want more detail.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Test one change at a time.
- Decide what success means before the test starts.
- Let the test run its planned length, even if one version looks ahead early.
- Test pages that many people actually visit.
- Write down what you learned, including tests that showed no difference.

**Avoid:**
- Stopping a test the moment one version pulls ahead.
- Testing several changes together and then guessing which one worked.
- Running a test during an unusual sale or a major ad push.
- Testing pages that get very few visitors.
- Treating a single result as a rule for every page and every audience.

## Who A/B testing suits

Testing suits a store with steady traffic and a page that matters, such as a best selling product or a landing page that receives paid clicks. It also suits an owner whose designer and marketer disagree about a layout and who wants evidence instead of a debate. If your store is very new and traffic is light, we may suggest a conversion audit first, so your early changes rest on a clear review rather than a slow test.

## What we need from you

Tell us which page or element worries you most and what you hope to improve. We need access to your store and analytics as a collaborator, staff or team user, so we can build the versions and connect the goals. We never need your password. After you order, we reply with a short checklist and agree on the test before anything goes live.
